newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Distillate stocks seen in surplus in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Distillate stocks seen in surplus in APIs.

text.p: This evening's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) could show a year-over-year surplus in distillate stocks for the first time in more than a year even though a stock decline is seen.

"In this report we could very well have a positive distillate stock situation. We don't have the same declines expected that we had last year due to the weather," said William Brown, president of trading firm W.H. Brown & Co.
Dealers expect distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, to fall 2.6 million barrels.
The report reflects the week ended January 31. A year ago, distillate stocks declined five million barrels due to more severe winter conditions.
Crude stocks are expected to grow between two and three million barrels due to steady imports and a large amount of seasonal refinery maintenance cutting crude usage.
Utilization rates are expected to decrease by 0.5 percentage point after dropping a week earlier by 0.8 percentage point to 89.1 percent.
Gasoline stocks are also expected to grow between two and three million barrels.

"The anticipated three million barrel hike in gasoline supplies should exceed the the average increase as a continued strong pace of imports (350,000 to 450,000 barrels per day) offset another likely decline in refinery activity," said Sweeney Oil trader Jim Ritterbusch in a daily report.
A maintenance-related fall in refinery output is also being offset on the distillate side by milder weather, with slack heating oil demand tempering stock declines.
"It was just bloody cold last year compared to this year. If you look at the amount of heating degree days, there is just no comparison," said A.G. Edwards analyst Bill O'Grady.
Dealers noted on average, temperatures have been normal this winter in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.

Two extended winters in 1995 and 1996 left distillate stocks bare, with the year-over-year shortfall reaching 20 million barrels last August and sending heating oil prices to post-Gulf War highs in October.
However, high distillate output has replenished distillate stocks to near year ago levels. The last distillate surplus was a meager 522,000 barrels in June 1995.
"We could be entering a new period where distillate stocks remain above year ago levels," said trader William Brown.
